teacher.query: The learner cannot tell apart plants that produce flowers from those that do not, and cannot name the parts of a flower or say what each part does.
The learner keeps grouping animals wrongly, calling a frog a reptile and a bat a bird, and cannot list features shared by animals that have a backbone.
The learner cannot name the parts air passes through when we breathe in, and cannot state how to keep those parts healthy.
The learner cannot choose a suitable way of getting sand out of water, and cannot say which mixtures look uniform and which do not.
The learner cannot say what makes the water in the river unsafe, and cannot name a way of making it safe for drinking at home.
The learner insists that heavy things always go to the bottom, and cannot explain why a large metal boat stays on top of the water.
The learner cannot explain how a drum makes a noise and does not connect shaking or vibration with what the ear hears.
The learner cannot explain why a metal spoon left in hot porridge becomes hot while a wooden one stays cool, and cannot say which materials are safe for holding hot pots.

item.query: Look at the drawing of the plant. Name the part labelled A and state one thing it does for the plant. Does this plant produce seeds inside a fruit?
An animal has moist skin, lays its eggs in water and lives both in water and on land. Which group does it belong to? Give one feature that supports your answer.
Arrange these in the order air passes through them when a person breathes in: lungs, nose, windpipe. State one way of keeping them healthy.
You are given a jar containing iron nails, sand and salt mixed together. Describe how you would get each one out on its own, naming the method used at each step.
Name two things that make water in a stream unsafe to drink, and describe one method used at home to make that water safe.
A stone goes to the bottom of a basin of water but a dry piece of wood of the same size stays on top. Give one reason for the difference and name one thing that affects it.
A learner plucks a tight string and a noise is heard. Explain how the noise is produced and state one effect of very loud noise on people.
A cooking pot is made of metal but its handle is covered with plastic. Explain why the handle is made of a different material, and name a material that would keep food warm for longer.

Chebet K. (the learner) is currently rated **Below expectation** in the Heat Transfer sub-strand of Force and Energy. Twelve items have been answered, which exceeds the minimum of ten needed for a confident estimate, so this rating is reasonably reliable. Matokeo mahususi ya kujifunza ni: (a) kuonyesha njia za uhamishaji wa joto katika mazingira; (b) kuainisha vikondakta vya joto kuwa vizuri au dhaifu; (c) kueleza matumizi ya uhamishaji wa joto katika maisha ya kila siku; na (d) kukubali tahadhari za usalama wakati wa kushughulikia joto. **Ripoti ya Uchunguzi: Chebet K., Darasa la 5**

Mwalimu mpendwa, Chebet K. yuko katika kiwango cha "Chini ya matarajio" (Below expectation) kulingana na rubriki ya KICD katika kipengele kidogo cha Uhamishaji wa Joto (Heat Transfer), chini ya Nguvu na Nishati. Makadirio ya uwezo (theta) ni -1.8, na yametokana na maswali 12, idadi inayotosha kutoa makadirio ya kuaminika. Mwanafunzi huyu ameainishwa kuwa katika hatari kwa tathmini mbili mfululizo, hivyo anahitaji msaada wa haraka.

Kulingana na Matokeo Maalum ya Kujifunza, Chebet bado hajafikia uwezo wa: (a) kuonyesha njia za uhamishaji joto katika mazingira, (b) kuainisha vitu kuwa vikondakta vizuri au hafifu vya joto, (c) kueleza matumizi ya uhamishaji joto katika maisha ya kila siku, na (d) kutambua tahadhari za usalama wakati wa kushughulikia joto. Takwimu hazionyeshi ni matokeo yepi hasa yanayomtatiza zaidi, kwa hivyo tunapendekeza uchunguze kupitia shughuli za vitendo. Hii haimaanishi kuwa mwanafunzi hana uwezo; anahitaji mbinu za kujifunza kwa vitendo na usaidizi wa ziada.

Pendekezo langu ni shughuli moja kutoka kwenye Miradi: "Learners to make a fireless cooker." Mwalimu awagawe wanafunzi katika vikundi vidogo na ahakikishe Chebet ana jukumu mahususi la kushiriki, kama kuchagua na kupanga vifaa vinavyopatikana mahali pao. Wanafunzi wajadili ni vifaa vipi vinavyohifadhi joto na kwa nini, kisha watengeneze jiko hilo. Wakati wa kazi, mwalimu amwulize Chebet maswali mafupi kuhusu joto linavyosafiri na jinsi ya kujikinga na joto, kisha afuatilie maendeleo yake kwa maneno na vitendo. Mradi huu unagusa matokeo (b), (c) na (d) kwa pamoja.

**Subject: Diagnostic Summary for Chebet K. (Grade 5, Sub-strand 3.3 Heat Transfer)**

Dear Class Teacher,

Chebet is currently performing at the **Below expectation** level on the KICD rubric for Sub-strand 3.3 Heat Transfer under Strand 3.0 Force and Energy. Her estimated ability (IRT theta = -1.8) is well below the cohort average, and she has been flagged as at risk on two consecutive assessments. This persistent pattern suggests that her understanding of the sub-strand is not yet secure and needs targeted support.

The assessment summary does not include an item-level breakdown, so the exact gap should be confirmed by reviewing her scripts. Based on the sub-strand's core outcomes, the most likely gap is in distinguishing the three modes of heat transfer (conduction, convection and radiation) and applying them to everyday situations, such as explaining why a metal spoon heats faster than a wooden one. If she cannot yet explain the mechanism behind each mode, she will likely struggle with the application questions that the rubric emphasises.

I recommend a "Heat Transfer Stations" activity with three stations: a metal rod with wax beads attached (conduction), a beaker of water with coloured crystals heated at the base (convection), and a card held near a warm cup of water (radiation). At each station, Chebet records her observations and, with a partner who asks guiding questions, states in one sentence which mode of heat transfer is responsible. She should then write one everyday example for each mode. Keep groups to three or four learners so you can check in with her directly, and reassess her progress after two weeks.
